mainTopic: The mixed-up sons of a כהנת and her slave woman, and who may receive תרומה at the granary and why.
overview: The amud opens at the end of a משנה about two babies who got mixed up: the son of a כהנת and the son of her slave woman. Since no one knows which is which, the משנה rules that before they are freed they may not marry at all. Once they grow up and free each other, they may marry women fit for כהונה. Each is then treated with the strict rules of both a כהן and a ישראל: he avoids impurity from the dead and does not eat תרומה, but he is never punished, made to pay, or stripped of what is his. The גמרא then fixes the משנה's wording in two places: 'the certain ones died' instead of 'the unflawed ones,' and 'a share together' instead of 'one share.' It also explains why חליצה must come before יבום. The 'share together' reading follows רבי יהודה, who says a slave gets תרומה only when his master is with him. The גמרא explains that this depended on local custom: in רבי יהודה's town, getting תרומה counted as proof of being a כהן. A story about רבי אלעזר בר צדוק shows how this almost made a slave into a כהן. Finally, a ברייתא lists ten people who are not handed תרומה at the threshing floor, and the גמרא begins explaining the reasons, continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: Before they are freed: no corpse impurity and no marriage at all
steps.stepSummary: Each mixed-up son may not become impure from the dead and may not marry any woman, fit or unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: They may not become impure from the dead. They may not marry women, neither fit women nor unfit women.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the limits on the two mixed-up sons while they are still in their mixed-up state.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each son might be a כהן, so he must avoid impurity from the dead. He also can't marry anyone: a slave may not marry a fit Jewish woman, and a כהן may not marry a woman unfit for כהונה. Since either one might be either, every kind of marriage is blocked.

keyTerms.meaning: becoming impure from a dead body (forbidden to a כהן)
women fit to marry a כהן
women unfit to marry a כהן
a doubt; a case where we don't know which way it is

steps.confusionAlert: "Fit" and "unfit" here are about marrying into כהונה. The fit women are blocked because one son might be a slave. The unfit women are blocked because one son might be a כהן.

phrases.english: And they may not become impure from the dead.
phrases.notes: "They" are the two mixed-up sons from earlier in the משנה: the כהנת's son and her slave woman's son.

phrases.english: And they may not marry women,
whether fit ones or unfit ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier part of the משנה describing the mixed-up sons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While they are mixed-up, each is barred from corpse impurity and from any marriage.

steps.title: After they grow up and free each other, they may marry fit women
steps.stepSummary: Once each frees the other, they may marry women fit for כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the mixed-up ones grew up and freed each other, they may marry women who are fit for the priesthood.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a fix: when the two grow up, each one frees the other, and this opens the door to marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since each frees the other, whoever was the slave is now a freed slave, and a freed slave may marry a fit Jewish woman. A woman fit for כהונה is also fine for the one who is a כהן. So this kind of woman works no matter which son is which.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up everything that follows: from here on the משנה describes the two after they were freed, when each is either a כהן or a ישראל (a freed slave).

phrases.english: If the mixed-up ones grew up
and freed each other,
they may marry women fit for the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִגְדִּילוּ הַתַּעֲרוֹבוֹת וְשִׁחְרְרוּ זֶה אֶת זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a solution to the marriage problem raised in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After freeing each other, they may marry women fit for כהונה.

steps.title: No corpse impurity, but no lashes if they did become impure
steps.stepSummary: They must avoid impurity from the dead, but if they became impure they don't get lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: They may not become impure from the dead, and if they did become impure, they do not get the forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now lists the rules for the freed pair, starting with impurity from the dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since each might be a כהן, he should be strict and stay away from the dead. But lashes are only given when we know for sure a sin was done, and each might be a ישראל, so no lashes are given.

phrases.english: And they may not become impure from the dead,
and if they became impure,
they do not receive the forty lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the list of rules for the two after they were freed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forbidden to become impure from the dead, but no lashes if they did.

steps.title: No eating תרומה, but no payment if they ate it
steps.stepSummary: They may not eat תרומה, but if they did, they don't pay back the value plus a fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: They may not eat תרומה, and if they ate it, they do not pay the principal and the added fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same pattern to תרומה: be strict at the start, but no penalty afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that one of them is a freed slave, who is a ישראל, he may no longer eat תרומה, and we don't know which one he is. Someone who is not a כהן and eats תרומה by mistake pays קרן וחומש. Here each one might be a כהן, so we can't make him pay.

keyTerms.meaning: the portion of produce given to a כהן
the principal (the value of what was eaten)
an added fifth paid as a penalty

phrases.english: And they may not eat תרומה,
and if they ate it,
they do not pay the principal and the fifth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 3, now for תרומה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forbidden to eat תרומה, but no קרן וחומש if they did.

steps.title: No share of תרומה at the granary, but they keep their own תרומה money
steps.stepSummary: They don't get תרומה handed out at the granary, but they may sell the תרומה from their own crops and keep the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not get a share at the granary. But they may sell the תרומה, and the money belongs to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what happens with תרומה, both when they want to receive it and when they have their own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To get תרומה from others at the granary, a person must show he is a כהן, and neither one can show that. But no one can prove either one is not a כהן either, so no כהן can take their own תרומה away from them. They can't eat it, but they may sell it to a כהן and keep the money.

keyTerms.meaning: the granary, where תרומה was given out

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases: getting תרומה from others is not allowed, but keeping the value of their own תרומה is allowed. Both come from the same doubt.

phrases.english: And they do not receive a share at the granary.
But they may sell the תרומה,
phrases.notes: This is the תרומה separated from their own crops, which they may not eat themselves.

phrases.english: and the money is theirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the תרומה rules, from eating to receiving and owning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No share at the granary, but they keep the money from their own תרומה.

steps.title: No share in Temple offerings, but what is theirs stays theirs
steps.stepSummary: They don't share in קדשים and aren't given offerings, but nothing of their own is taken from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not get a share of the Temple's holy offerings, and holy offerings are not given to them. But what is theirs is not taken out of their hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same thinking to the holy offerings of the Temple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each one might not be a כהן, so he doesn't get a portion of the offerings and isn't handed offerings to bring. But since no one can prove he isn't a כהן, the parts of his own offerings that would go to a כהן are not taken from him.

keyTerms.meaning: the holy offerings of the Temple

phrases.english: And they do not receive a share of the Temple's holy offerings,
and holy offerings are not given to them.
But what is theirs is not taken out of their hands.
phrases.notes: That's the parts of their own offerings that would normally go to a כהן, like the hides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 5, now for Temple offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No share in קדשים and none given to them, but their own portions are not taken.

steps.title: Exempt from the meat gifts; their בכור grazes until it gets a blemish
steps.stepSummary: They don't give the foreleg, jaw, and maw to a כהן, and their firstborn animal is left until it becomes blemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are exempt from giving the foreleg, the jaws, and the maw. And his firstborn animal should graze until it becomes blemished.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה covers the gifts a ישראל gives a כהן from his animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן can't demand the meat gifts from them, because each might be a כהן himself, and a כהן doesn't have to give them. With a בכור, he isn't made to hand it over to a כהן to be brought as an offering. It is left to graze until it gets a blemish, and then he may keep it, since no one can prove he isn't a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: the foreleg (a gift to the כהן)
the jaws (a gift to the כהן)
the maw, or stomach (a gift to the כהן)
a firstborn animal, holy and given to a כהן
becomes blemished, so it can't be an offering

phrases.english: And they are exempt from the foreleg
and from the jaws and from the maw,
and his firstborn animal should graze
until it becomes blemished.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְטוּרִין מִן הַזְּרוֹעַ וּמִן הַלְּחָיַיִם וּמִן הַקֵּיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from Temple offerings to the gifts from ordinary animals and the בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Exempt from the meat gifts; the בכור stays with him until it is blemished.

steps.title: The general rule: strict rules of both כהנים and ישראלים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums it up: we put on him the strict rules of a כהן and the strict rules of a ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we place on him the strict rules of priests and the strict rules of Israelites.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with the principle that explains every rule before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wherever being a כהן would make things stricter (like avoiding the dead or blocked marriages), he keeps it. Wherever being a ישראל would make things stricter (like not eating תרומה or not getting a share), he keeps that too. Each gets the strict side of both.
steps.whatToRemember: A person who is a ספק כהן is treated strictly both ways. He can't be punished or made to pay, and nothing can be taken from him, because no one can prove what he is.

phrases.english: And we place on him the strict rules of priests
and the strict rules of Israelites.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנוֹתְנִין עָלָיו חוּמְרֵי כֹהֲנִים וְחוּמְרֵי יִשְׂרְאֵלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up all the rules listed before it under one principle.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The mixed-up sons get the strict rules of both כהנים and ישראלים.

steps.title: Are the mixed-up sons really unfit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'if the כשרים died' and asks whether this means the mixed-up sons are unfit just because they got mixed up.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה said 'if the unflawed ones died, etc.' But are these mixed-up sons unfit just because they got mixed up?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה. Calling the other sons 'כשרים' (unflawed) suggests that the mixed-up sons are flawed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being mixed up only means we don't know whose son each one is. It is not a flaw in his lineage. So the word כשרים seems to be the wrong word.

keyTerms.meaning: Unflawed, fit (here: the sons whose lineage is known)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
'If the unflawed ones died, etc.'
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. The 'unflawed ones' are the sons whose mother is known for sure.

phrases.english: But these (mixed-up sons),
just because they got mixed up,
are they unfit?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָנָךְ, מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיעָרוּב לְהוּ הָווּ לְהוּ פְּסוּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's discussion of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Calling the known sons 'כשרים' wrongly suggests the mixed-up sons are flawed, but being mixed up is not a flaw.

steps.title: Read it as 'the certain ones died'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא changes the wording to 'the certain sons died.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Say instead: 'And the certain ones died.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers by fixing the wording of the משנה so it no longer suggests the mixed-up sons are flawed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ודאין' (the certain ones) just means the sons whose mother we know. It describes what we know, not their status, so the challenge goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (a way of fixing the wording)
The certain ones, whose lineage is known

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
Say: 'And the certain ones died.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה calls the mixed-up sons flawed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only means the sons whose lineage is known died.

steps.title: חליצה must come before יבום
steps.stepSummary: With the widows of the daughter-in-law's certain sons, one mixed-up son must do חליצה first, and only then can the other do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'With the widows of the daughter-in-law's sons, one does חליצה, etc.' Only if he does חליצה first and then the other does יבום. But not יבום first, because he might be sleeping with a יבמה who is still bound, as if he were an outsider.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains an order the משנה requires: חליצה first, then יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each mixed-up son may or may not be the real brother. If one did יבום first and he was not the brother, he would be with a woman still tied to her real brother-in-law. After חליצה by the first son, she is freed either way, so the second can safely do יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: To do יבום, marrying the brother's widow
A יבמה with someone from outside the family, which is forbidden

phrases.english: 'With the sons of the daughter-in-law, one does חליצה, etc.'
phrases.notes: He means the widows of the daughter-in-law's known sons, who died.

phrases.english: Specifically, first doing חליצה and then doing יבום,
but doing יבום first, no,
because he would be breaching the ban on a יבמה with an outsider.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חליצה must come first. יבום first is not allowed, because of the risk of יבמה לשוק.

steps.title: Why say 'one share'? It's obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the כהנת whose child was mixed up and asks why it needs to say they get one share.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A כהנת whose child was mixed up, etc.' — they get one share. Isn't one share obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's words 'one share' as stating the obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each mixed-up child is either a כהן or a כהן's slave, so each one gets only one share of תרומה. Why would the משנה need to tell us that?

keyTerms.meaning: A woman from a כהן family

phrases.english: 'A כהנת whose (child) was mixed up, etc.'
phrases.notes: Her child was mixed up with her maidservant's child. This line comes from an earlier part of the משנה.

phrases.english: 'One share' is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to another phrase from the earlier part of the משנה, about the mixed-up children of a כהנת and her maidservant receiving תרומה at the granary.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Of course each one gets only one share. The משנה would not need to say it.

steps.title: Read it as 'a share together'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording to 'חלק כאחד': they get a share only if they come together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'A share together.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the משנה as 'a share together.' This means the two mixed-up children get תרומה at the granary only when they come as a pair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the משנה teaches something new. Either one alone might be a slave without his master. When they come together, one is surely the כהן and the other is surely his slave.
steps.confusionAlert: The point of 'כאחד' is not how many shares they get. It means they receive תרומה at the granary only when both come together.

phrases.english: Say: 'a share together.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is saying the obvious: one share.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means they receive a share only when they come together.

steps.title: This fits the view that a slave needs his master present
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that, with this new wording, the משנה follows the view that a slave gets תרומה only if his master is with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned this in the משנה like the one who says: We do not hand out תרומה to a slave unless his master is with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out which opinion the fixed wording of the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying they get תרומה only together means a possible slave alone gets nothing. That only makes sense if a slave needs his master present to receive תרומה.

phrases.english: We learned (in the משנה) like the one who says:
We do not hand out תרומה to a slave
unless his master is with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a result from the fixed wording in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה, read as 'חלק כאחד', follows the view that a slave gets תרומה only with his master.

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי disagree
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the dispute. רבי יהודה says a slave needs his master with him. רבי יוסי says the doubtful one can claim his share either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: We do not hand out תרומה to a slave unless his master is with him. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: He can say, 'If I am a כהן, give me for my own sake. And if I am a כהן's slave, give me for my master's sake.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show where the view in step 14 comes from. It shows that this view belongs to רבי יהודה, and that רבי יוסי disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, a mixed-up child who comes alone might be a slave without his master, so he gets nothing. According to רבי יוסי, he wins either way, so he gets a share even alone. So the משנה's 'חלק כאחד' matches only רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
These are the words of רבי יהודה

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה says the mixed-up children get תרומה only together, and that follows רבי יהודה (a slave needs his master present). רבי יוסי would give each one a share even alone, since 'either way I deserve it.'

phrases.english: As it was taught: We do not hand out תרומה to a slave
unless his master is with him.
These are the words of רבי יהודה.
רבי יוסי says: He can say,

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֹּהֵן אֲנִי — תְּנוּ לִי בִּשְׁבִיל עַצְמִי,
phrases.english: 'If I am a כהן, give me for my own sake,
phrases.notes: The speaker is the one whose status is in doubt, like the mixed-up child, who might be a כהן or a כהן's slave.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם עֶבֶד כֹּהֵן אֲנִי — תְּנוּ לִי בִּשְׁבִיל רַבִּי.
phrases.english: and if I am a כהן's slave, give me for my master's sake.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אֵין חוֹלְקִין תְּרוּמָה לְעֶבֶד אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן רַבּוֹ עִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the view mentioned in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That the view 'a slave needs his master present' belongs to רבי יהודה, and is disputed
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the משנה's ruling about the mixed-up children follows רבי יהודה, not רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The dispute depends on local custom
steps.stepSummary: In רבי יהודה's place, getting תרומה counted as proof of being a כהן. In רבי יוסי's place, it did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: In רבי יהודה's place, people would treat someone who got תרומה as a proven כהן for family-lineage purposes. In רבי יוסי's place, they would not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind the argument from Step 15. רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי each followed the custom of their own town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If getting תרומה makes people assume you are a כהן, then a slave taking תרומה alone could later be treated as a כהן by mistake. That is why רבי יהודה requires the master to be there. In רבי יוסי's town there was no such risk, so the slave could take his share alone.

keyTerms.meaning: his place or town, where that חכם's ruling was followed
they raise up, meaning they give someone the status of a כהן
family lineage, meaning proven status as a כהן for things like marriage

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an argument about whether a slave may eat תרומה. Both agree he may. The argument is whether letting him take it alone could later make people wrongly think he is a כהן.

phrases.english: In Rabbi Yehuda's place
they would raise someone from teruma to lineage.
phrases.notes: If people saw you get תרומה, they treated it as proof that your family is כהנים.

phrases.english: In Rabbi Yosei's place
they would not raise someone from teruma to lineage.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּמְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָיוּ מַעֲלִין מִתְּרוּמָה לְיוּחֲסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the dispute quoted in the ברייתא of Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is based on custom. Where תרומה proves כהונה, a slave needs his master with him. Where it does not, he can take his share alone.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בר צדוק's single testimony
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבי אלעזר בר צדוק testified only once, and because of it a slave was raised to כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר בר צדוק said, 'In all my life I testified only one time, and because of my words they raised a slave to כהונה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a real story. It shows how getting תרומה could lead to someone being treated as a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story shows that the worry in Step 16 is real. Testimony that someone got תרומה could end with a slave being treated as a כהן. As written, though, the story says this actually happened, and the גמרא is about to question that.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok said:
In all my days I never testified
except for one testimony,
and they raised a slave to the priesthood based on my word.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example of the danger described in Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That testimony about receiving תרומה could lead to a slave being treated as a כהן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי אלעזר בר צדוק about his one testimony.

steps.title: Could a צדיק really cause such a mistake?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that ה׳ does not let even the animals of צדיקים cause a mistake, so surely the צדיקים themselves would not cause one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think they raised him? ה׳ does not bring a mistake through even the animals of צדיקים. Surely He would not bring one through the צדיקים themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא. It cannot be that a צדיק like רבי אלעזר בר צדוק actually caused a slave to become a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a קל וחומר. If ה׳ protects even a צדיק's animal from causing a sin, He would surely protect the צדיק himself. So the words 'they raised' cannot be read literally.

keyTerms.meaning: could it enter your mind? (meaning: that can't be right)
a stumbling block, a mistake that leads to sin

phrases.english: Could it enter your mind that they actually raised him?!
Now, if through the animals of the righteous

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מֵבִיא תַּקָּלָה עַל יָדָן,
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not bring a stumbling block,
then the righteous themselves, all the more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the literal wording of the ברייתא in Step 17.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר‎: ה׳ protects even צדיקים' animals from causing sin, so He would surely not let a צדיק cause a slave to be made a כהן.

steps.title: They only wanted to raise him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא: they only tried to raise the slave. He saw the man get תרומה in רבי יוסי's town and testified about it in רבי יהודה's town.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: they wanted to raise a slave to כהונה because of my words. He saw it in רבי יוסי's place, and then went and testified in רבי יהודה's place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by changing the wording. The mistake almost happened, but it did not actually happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יוסי's town, giving a slave תרומה proved nothing, so seeing it there was harmless. But when he reported it in רבי יהודה's town, where תרומה proves כהונה, the court almost declared the slave a כהן. This also ties the story back to the local customs in Step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, say (the גמרא rereads the text)

steps.whatToRemember: Getting תרומה proved כהונה only in רבי יהודה's town. Testimony about something seen in רבי יוסי's town almost made a slave a כהן there, but it did not actually happen, because ה׳ protects צדיקים from causing such mistakes.

phrases.english: Rather, say:

phrases.aramaic: בִּקְּשׁוּ לְהַעֲלוֹת עֶבֶד לַכְּהוּנָּה עַל פִּי.
phrases.english: They sought to raise a slave to the priesthood based on my word.
He saw it in Rabbi Yosei's place,
phrases.notes: He saw a slave getting תרומה on his own, which was allowed there and proved nothing.

phrases.english: and went and testified in Rabbi Yehuda's place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: בִּקְּשׁוּ לְהַעֲלוֹת עֶבֶד לַכְּהוּנָּה עַל פִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 18 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording the text: 'they raised' becomes 'they sought to raise'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The slave was actually made a כהן because of רבי אלעזר בר צדוק's testimony.
steps.terutzMaskana: The court only tried to do it. The mix-up came from testimony about something seen in רבי יוסי's town being given in רבי יהודה's town.

steps.title: Ten people who do not get תרומה at the threshing floor
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists ten people who are not given תרומה in public at the threshing floor. Most of them may still have it sent to their homes, but not a טמא or one who married a woman unfit for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: there are ten people who are not given תרומה at the threshing floor. They are a חרש, a שוטה, a קטן, a טומטום, an אנדרוגינוס, a slave, a woman, an ערל, a טמא, and a man who married a woman forbidden to him. All of them may have it sent to their homes, except the טמא and the man who married a forbidden woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that lists ten people who are not handed תרומה at the threshing floor. It then says that most of them may have it sent home anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that getting תרומה at the threshing floor could count as proof of being a כהן. This ברייתא adds two levels. Some people are only kept from the public handout but still get תרומה at home. Two people, the טמא and the man in a forbidden marriage, get none at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The threshing floor, where תרומה was handed out in public
A person whose body does not clearly show male or female
A person with both male and female features
Not fitting for him, meaning a woman a כהן may not marry
They send it, meaning to the person's home

steps.confusionAlert: Not getting תרומה at the threshing floor does not mean the person may not eat תרומה. For most of the list, the only issue is the public handout, because they still get it at home.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
There are ten to whom we do not hand out תרומה
at the threshing floor,
and these are they: a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor,
a tumtum, and a hermaphrodite,
and the slave, and the woman, and the uncircumcised man, and the impure man,
phrases.notes: He means the slave of a כהן and a woman from a כהן's family, people who are allowed to eat תרומה.

phrases.english: and one who marries a woman who is unfit for him.
And to all of them we send it to their homes,
except for the impure man
and one who marries a woman who is unfit for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עֲשָׂרָה אֵין חוֹלְקִין לָהֶם תְּרוּמָה בְּבֵית הַגֳּרָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story of the slave raised to כהונה to a general ברייתא about who receives תרומה at the threshing floor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ten people are not given תרומה at the threshing floor. Eight of them may have it sent home. The טמא and the man in a forbidden marriage get none.

steps.title: Starting to explain the reasons behind the list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins with the easy cases. A חרש, שוטה, and קטן lack understanding, so it makes sense not to hand them תרומה in public. It then starts to say the same about a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for a חרש, a שוטה, and a קטן, because they do not have full understanding. A טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are also understandable…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a question. It first lists the items on the list that are easy to explain, so it can then ask about the ones that are hard to explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בשלמא means "granted, this one is fine." The חרש, שוטה, and קטן lack understanding, so a public handout to them is not fitting. The sentence about the טומטום and אנדרוגינוס is not finished yet. The real question will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this case makes sense (opens a question about a harder case)

phrases.english: Granted, a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor:
they are not people of full understanding.
A tumtum and a hermaphrodite also:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins asking for the reasons behind the ברייתא's list in Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why each of the ten is kept from the public handout. The easy cases are explained first, to set up a question about the harder ones.
